html:
The Forest Brothers were armed partisans who fought Soviet rule in Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia from 1944 into the 1950s. The movement was largest in Lithuania, where tens of thousands took part.

They hid in forests and bunkers, attacked Soviet officials and collaborators, and hoped the Western powers would come to their aid. They never did. The Soviet security forces wore them down with informers and the mass deportations that took away their families and supporters.

Most resistance ended by 1953. The last known Estonian partisan was found in 1978. Thousands died on each side. After independence the partisans were honoured as heroes in Lithuania, and their leader Jonas Žemaitis was recognised as a head of state. See the Soviet Union.
sum: The Forest Brothers were armed partisans who fought Soviet rule in Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia from 1944 into the 1950s. The movement was largest in Lithuania, where tens of thousands took part.
